description.narrative: Community Stabilization by establishing functional and effective community-level conflict resolution and prevention structures in Kubum and Edfursan localities, South Darfur State.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

description.narrative: - Functional and effective community-level conflict resolution and prevention structures in Kubum and Edfursan established. - Capacity of women to meaningfully participate in local and state level peace building platforms enhanced.

comment.narrative:
Output 2: Ensure peace dividends for community interdependence and co-existence are delivered through diverse livelihoods options and effective natural resource management:
1. Community savings groups: - 9 Groups - 215 (133 women, 82men): 2,260,000 SDG (approx. US$3,964) – savings 1,050,000 (approx. US$1,842) - loans.
2. Income Generating Activities (IGAs): - 6 Groups - 30 members (15 men & 15 women): Food processing, tailoring and motorcycle business. 4 motorbikes were distributed to 2 groups in Alhuda and Markundi during this reporting period. 2 more motorbikes will be distributed in the next reporting period. The motorbikes will help the members to generate income through transportation of goods during harvest season and beyond.

2021-2022 Targets:
Output 1: Community based conflict resolution and reconciliation mechanisms are in use and working effectively to resolve conflicts: - Formation, training and equipping of 3 CBRMs targeting the three main areas of Nurley, Alhuda and Markundi. - Identify, select and train peace committees on conflict resolution, peace building and community cohesion. - empower women and women groups especially Hakkama and re-define their role to become peace ambassadors. - Enhance the role of faith leaders through capacity building to become champions of peace and inclusion. - Link the CBRMs to the newly created Observatory of Violence based at Nyala University to provide advice on the new trends of creating community harmony and building durable peace.
Output 2: Peace Dividends for community inter-dependence and co-existence delivered: - Construct market shades at Nurley administration unit for different tribes to carry out their trading and generate livelihoods. - Support the vulnerable groups such as youths and women with IGAs. - Provide women vocational training and equipment to improve their life skills and support them with start-up kits to further develop their skills. - Inculcate saving and lending culture through the S4T training as well as follow ups. - Provide clean water for domestic and livestock use through the Nurley and Alhuda water scheme rehabilitation as well as broken hand pumps. - Demarcate migratory route passing through three administrative units in-order to reduce human livestock conflicts. - Construct school and Women and Girls safe spaces to support education and recreational facilities as well as rehabilitation of a health facility to support the health status of the communities.
Output 3: Women Organizations, including those representing pastoralist women, empowered to meaningfully participate in local and state level peace building platforms: - Establish women CSOs and provide them with small grants to take part in local level peace building. - Train young women to become advocates of GBV and train men to become GBV ambassadors. - Establish GBV desks in police stations and train their officers to ensure the fight against GBV. - Carry out mapping for referral pathways while training for medical personnel on clinical management of rape will be carried out as part of case management. - Provide support for Child Protection and GBV coordination meetings at the locality level.
Output 4: Improved networking, coordination and learning between local and state level peace building institutions: - Support the CBRMs and Community leaders to participate in National Peace Building Forums. - Support joint research, documentation and dissemination of Conflict information on progress at state and locality levels with Peace Research Centre at Nyala University. - Support engagement of CBRMs and state governance apparatus that includes the police in management of conflicts. - Students from Nyala University to provide accompaniment to the CBRMs for capacity building. - Carry out joint research and publication with Nyala University Peace Studies and Research Centre.

• 3 CBRMs formed – one in each of the 3 villages of project implementation (60 members). • Conducted assessment for Alhuda and Nurly water system, identified the needed spare parts for rehabilitation. • Requested the Spare parts through our procurement system. • Developed MOU with Nyala University Peace Studies and Research Centre to collaborate to implement some of activities
